---
title: "Ensemble learning"
subtitle: "Model averaging and SuperLearner"
date: "Nov 20, 2026"
date-format: long
---

Why combining models helps: ensemble risk equals average risk minus diversity; model averaging with weights; SuperLearner (stacking) with cross-validated predictions and a meta-learner. Bagging, random forests and boosting (Lecture 10) are the tree-based members of this family.

📖 **Assigned reading:** ISLR §8.2

## 🧪 Lab

Live, in-browser R lab — runs entirely in your browser via webR, no local R install needed.

- 🧪 [Lab: Bike-share demand (live R)](code/class11_lab1.html){target="_blank"} — fit five different models, then combine them by averaging and by stacking (SuperLearner). Check the identity *ensemble risk = average risk − diversity* on real data, and see when a combination beats the best single model and when it does not.
